source.name: Desuarchive /g/ scrape, Jan 2019 to Sept 2026
source.short-desc: Our own Hayden scrape of Desuarchive's /g/ 2019-2026, text only, published as per-year tarballs of thread.json
source.capture:
OUR OWN SCRAPE, published to IA 2026-10-05 as the finished version of what was the hand-copied `hayden-desuarchive` work in progress. Scraped with a Hayden fork (https://github.com/laine-hallot/Hayden/tree/0b84bf001036a1721995d700324375e7940b643b) against Desuarchive's FoolFuuka API -- every record carries a doc_id and desu-usergeneratedcontent.xyz media links, so the upstream is Desuarchive, not 4chan itself. Covers every /g/ thread 2019-01-01 EST to 2026-09-07 EDT, which no public dump covers: desuarchive_db_201909 ends in 2019 and nothing else in the registry picks /g/ up after that. TEXT ONLY, no images. Runs went one year at a time, newest year first, threads within a year oldest first; a re-scrape would differ slightly because of moderation on Desuarchive since.

PAYLOAD: one 8.2GB file, desu-archive-scrape-jan-01-2019-sept-07-2026.tar.gz, plus IA bookkeeping. Surveyed against archive.org/metadata (5 files); no image payloads, so no download.exclude. It is a TARBALL OF TARBALLS: desu-archive-scrape-jan-01-2019-sept-07-2026/ holding g-2019.tar.gz ... g-2026.tar.gz (g-2019 alone is 960MB) and logs/ (the scraper's run logs). Each year unpacks to g-<year>/g/<threadno>/thread.json plus an empty thumbs/ per thread, and some years carry Hayden's own hayden/ state directory, which is not a board. Threads were sorted into years by the OP's EST post date after scraping, since the first runs shared one output directory. The prepare script unpacks both levels into extracted/ (stamped per tarball) and converts every g-<year> root to out/<board>/posts.ndjson (staging-json's hayden-to-ndjson).

FORMAT: thread.json is Hayden's envelope, {Thread: {ThreadId, IsArchived, Posts[], OriginalObject: {posts}, AdditionalMetadata: {Deleted, Sticky, Locked}}, ThreadDeleted, DeletedPostIds}. Each post carries Hayden's normalised fields (PostNumber, TimePosted, Author, Tripcode, ContentRaw, ContentType, IsDeleted, Media[]) and the upstream FoolFuuka record verbatim in OriginalObject: doc_id, num, subnum, thread_num, timestamp, name, trip, title, comment_sanitized, poster_country_name, capcode, sticky, locked, deleted, media {media, media_filename, media_hash, media_link, thumb_link, media_size, exif}. THE CONVERTER READS OriginalObject, NOT HAYDEN'S FIELDS: the envelope has no Subject at all (15,010 of the sample's posts had a title, and only the upstream record carried it), and ContentRaw trims trailing whitespace (8 posts differed from comment_sanitized by exactly that). ContentType is 1 on every post.

TIMESTAMP IS TRUE UTC, so the converter copies it untouched. Measured against 4chan's own tim upload time (UTC milliseconds, preserved in media.exif): for all 377,508 media posts in the sample, tim/1e6 - timestamp was 0 or 1 second. New York wall time would have been off by 4-5 hours. Hayden's TimePosted (ISO 8601, +00:00) equals it exactly on every post, but is derived from it rather than independent evidence.

COMMENT is comment_sanitized, which is Asagi plain text: '>' is literal, [code] and [spoiler] are Asagi's own tags (6,966 and 5 posts), the same convention the SQL sources stage. The 24 comments containing '<span', '<a href', '>' etc. are users typing markup literally. There is no `comment` field -- Desuarchive's API returns only the sanitized variant. Empty comments are '' in the record (51,306 in the sample) and Hayden omits ContentRaw for them.

TIMESTAMP IS TRUE UTC, so the converter copies it untouched. Measured on the 2026 work-in-progress sample against 4chan's own tim upload time (UTC milliseconds, preserved in media.exif): for all 377,508 media posts, tim/1e6 - timestamp was 0 or 1 second. New York wall time would have been off by 4-5 hours. Hayden's TimePosted (ISO 8601, +00:00) equals it exactly on every post, but is derived from it rather than independent evidence. NOT YET CHECKED ON 2019-2025: the API served UTC for /mlp/ back to 2012 (see desuarchive_mlp_1_42799493_20251114215436), so the same is expected, but the tim check should be repeated on an early year after staging.

OVERLAPS desuarchive_db_201909 for /g/ Jan-Sep 2019, and the same posts appear in both. Since posts are first-writer-wins, ingest order decides which copy survives there.

WORK-IN-PROGRESS SAMPLE (data/my-archive-1, 2.8GB, surveyed 2026-09-11): 38,044 threads, 2,029,716 posts, all 2026-01-01 to 2026-09-11 UTC. 37,859 /g/ threads (2,026,407 posts) and 185 /his/ threads (3,309 posts) -- /his/ is staged too; a partial capture never blocks a fuller one. 32,312 posts flagged deleted (kept, as the SQL sources keep their _deleted companions); 5,045 threads with AdditionalMetadata.Deleted. No ghost posts (subnum always 0), capcode N on all but 68 (M). Every thread's first post is its OP, every record's thread_num matches its directory, no post number repeats within a thread. poster_country_name is the string 'False' throughout. Media posts have exactly one media entry; Hayden's Media[0] agrees with OriginalObject.media on filename and hash in every case. That sample is a subset of g-2026 and was staged under the old hayden-desuarchive directory on the NAS, which this source does not read and which was never ingested.

RE-STAGING the conversion is a full pass: the converter has no notion of what it wrote last time. `prepare --force` re-runs it over everything in extracted/ (extraction itself is skipped unless a tarball is newer than its stamp).
